summary: Phase 4 Slice I (POST /api/auth/register + startup seed_admin dual-write to Mongo + Supabase Auth + public.profiles) verified GREEN end-to-end. Backend pytest: 38/38 PASS in test_iteration18_phase4i_register_supabase.py. (1) Fresh-email register with role=caregiver returns 200 with legacy access_token; Mongo users row created with hashed_password; Supabase Auth user created via POST /auth/v1/admin/users with the SAME UUID as Mongo and user_metadata={name,role}; public.profiles row mirrors id+email+name+role; legacy access_token authenticates GET /api/auth/me with the same id. (2) Immediately after register, the new user can sign in via Supabase password grant (POST {SUPABASE_URL}/auth/v1/token?grant_type=password) and the returned ES256 JWT authenticates GET /api/auth/me with the SAME id Mongo returned. (3) Duplicate-email (admin@healthguard.com) register returns 400 'Email already registered' and the existing Supabase admin uid 8f16fe69-... is NOT replaced (id stable before/after). (4) role='admin' register works identically: Supabase user_metadata.role='admin' and public.profiles.role='admin'; Supabase password grant succeeds. (5) Seeded users have matching UUIDs across all three stores: admin@healthguard.com -> 8f16fe69-b54e-421a-bfe5-e14900e7bacd in Mongo, Supabase Auth and PG profiles (role=admin); caregiver@healthguard.com -> 389b257d-7edb-4d12-adfc-3b8e80f91bf1 in all three (role=caregiver). Admin + caregiver can both login via BOTH legacy (Admin@123 / Caregiver@123) AND Supabase (AdminPassword123! / Caregiver123!), with the same user.id returned by /api/auth/login matching the canonical UUID. (6) Cleanup parity: a freshly registered user can be removed by DELETE {SUPABASE_URL}/auth/v1/admin/users/{uid} + Mongo delete_one — afterwards Mongo find returns None, Supabase admin list returns None, public.profiles count=0 (CASCADE on auth.users delete). (7) Phase 4 A-H regression GREEN: 10 endpoints (/api/auth/me, /api/caregivers, /api/clients, /api/assignments, /api/documents, /api/shifts, /api/chat/threads, /api/onboarding?caregiver_id=389b257d..., /api/policies/acknowledgments, /api/training) x 2 admin JWTs (legacy HS256 from Admin@123 and Supabase ES256 from AdminPassword123!) = 20 parametrised tests all 200 OK with valid list/dict JSON bodies. (8) Frontend regression (Expo web, mobile 390x844, Supabase mode): admin@healthguard.com / AdminPassword123! -> Dashboard renders 'AUDIT READINESS 51%', OVERVIEW '1 Clients / 12 Caregivers / 50 Documents / 0 Trainings'; all 6 tabs (Dashboard/Documents/Team/Schedule/Policies/Assistant) load without any TypeError/ReferenceError/red-screen; Policies tab shows 'Your acknowledgments 2/20' with the baseline '01 - Code of Conduct - Acknowledged 6/22/2026, 4:04:55 AM' row. (9) Smoke test /app/scripts/_smoke_slice_i.py PASSES against the live backend (Mongo + Supabase Auth + profiles + Supabase login + duplicate rejection + cleanup cascade). (10) Final parity exactly preserved: PG profiles=13 == Mongo users=13, zero @phcp-smoke.io leftovers in either store.
action_items: (Optional, Slice J prep) server.py:54-78 register: hashed_password is still written to Mongo. Slice J should remove this column from Mongo writes (or stop reading it in login) and rely entirely on Supabase Auth for password verification. The Mongo row may then drop 'hashed_password' and only keep id/email/name/role/created_at.

(Optional) supa_data.create_supabase_auth_user returns False when Supabase admin POST /auth/v1/admin/users returns 422/already-registered. server.py register does NOT inspect that boolean — that's fine for the documented best-effort design, but worth keeping in mind for Slice J when strict mode is enabled.

(Optional) supa_data.create_supabase_auth_user upserts public.profiles defensively even though the on_auth_user_created trigger should populate it. If Slice J flips to 'strict', the explicit upsert can be removed once the trigger is verified reliable.

(Optional) /api/auth/register payload is logged via Uvicorn access log only — req.password is NOT logged. The Supabase admin POST in supa_data.create_supabase_auth_user sends the plaintext password over httpx; httpx logs are at WARNING level and won't include the body. Safe.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:54-78 register — Mongo insert_one is performed BEFORE the Supabase Auth call (line 68 then 71). This is the correct order for the best-effort design: if Supabase fails the user still has a legacy login. However, since create_supabase_auth_user explicitly passes 'id': uid (line 1128 in supa_data.py), the UUID stays in sync across stores. Verified by test_supabase_auth_user_has_same_uuid.

supa_data.create_supabase_auth_user lines 1119-1145 — try/except wraps the entire httpx call and never re-raises, satisfying 'Supabase outage = best-effort' requirement. The 422/already-registered branch (line 1138) returns False without logging at WARNING, so logs stay clean during dupe-registration attempts. The Bearer + apikey dual header pattern is correct for Supabase admin REST API.

supa_data.create_supabase_auth_user lines 1149-1161 — explicit profiles upsert is a defensive layer; combined with the on_auth_user_created trigger it provides at-least-once profile creation. INSERT...ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE keeps email/name/role authoritative from the register payload.

server.py:1626-1670 seed_admin — runs at startup, conditional on db.users.find_one to remain idempotent. After the Mongo upsert it calls supa_data.create_supabase_auth_user for BOTH admin (AdminPassword123!) AND caregiver (Caregiver123!) with the SAME UUIDs the Mongo rows use. Verified by TestSeededUserParity: admin uid 8f16fe69-... and caregiver uid 389b257d-... both match across Mongo, Supabase Auth, and public.profiles.
Pydantic EmailStr rejects reserved TLDs (.test/.example/.invalid/.localhost). Tests use @phcp-smoke.io. Required-credentials note from the review request is accurate and respected.

Backend duplicate-email check uses db.users.find_one({'email': req.email}) which is exact-match. If a user only exists in Supabase but not in Mongo (e.g., directly created via Supabase admin API), the register endpoint would NOT detect them and would attempt to re-create the Supabase user — which would return 422 already-registered and create_supabase_auth_user would return False. The Mongo row would still be created with a DIFFERENT UUID than the existing Supabase one. This is an edge case but documents the boundary of Slice I's 'Mongo is authoritative' design. Slice J's flip should consider checking Supabase Auth on top of Mongo to keep UUIDs in sync.
